kinds.finite-computation: checked by the programs in this repository on the user's download; the programs are not formally verified
kinds.independent-implementation: agreement with a separately written implementation on the same pinned input

not_claimed: anything about graph neural networks in general; no model was trained or tested
that a ball radius, or r_WL - r_min, is a number of GNN layers
anything about models that use species, coordinates, distances, angles or periodic labels
a maximum of r_min, r_WL or r_WL - r_min over the RCSR database; the 99 cases are a selection
that the graphs are the structures intended by the RCSR authors, beyond the stated source models
that nets whose balls agree up to some radius are the same net
a new isomorphism algorithm, a new concept, or priority
independent checking of the 93 non-core cases

claims.statement: For the six core cases of expected.json, a separately written implementation (Gemmi 0.7.5, NetworkX 3.7, Python standard library) computed the same r_min and r_WL from the same pinned 3dall.txt, and for fly V1 / ylf V1 the same counts of closed walks of length 10 (2,816,008 and 2,816,168).
claims.reproduce: python3 -B suite.py run --work work/core --scope core (this package; the independent code is not included)
claims.qualification: the independent team shared the definitions, the input and a description of the coordinate handling, but not the code or results; it built tsa/tsg without the ARC file

claims.statement: For each case in scope main, on the graphs built from the pinned 3dall.txt under the stated source models: the rooted balls of radius r_min - 1 are isomorphic (complete root-preserving map checked), the balls of radius r_min are not (certificate checked), and stable 1-WL with initial colours (distance from root, degree in ball) first separates the balls at radius r_WL (recomputed at every radius from 1 to r_WL).
claims.qualification: outside the six core cases, checked only by this package; the checker does not import the generator but shares algorithm.py and source_io.py with it and was written by the same team

claims.statement: The same statement as main-values holds for all 99 cases of expected.json when the optional RCSRnets.arc is supplied for nets whose coordinates do not give a graph under the source models. In 97 cases r_WL > r_min; the largest difference r_WL - r_min among the 99 is 4 (tsa V1 / tsg V3, r_min = 4, r_WL = 8).
claims.qualification: graphs from the ARC file assume a correspondence with the 3dall.txt record by net name, weighted 10-shell coordination sequence and a unique root; 10 of the 99 cases used such a graph in our runs; this scope is not run in CI

claims.statement: selftest.py runs 15 tests against a verified core work folder: corrupted input bytes, graph, isomorphism, walk count, WL sequence, schema and expected values, a removed certificate, a missing branch of a refutation tree (on two small hand-made graphs), a time limit, a simulated memory error, and a report path that would overwrite the input are each rejected with the documented exit code; a run without network from a local file and a run from a copy of only the manifest files both pass.
claims.qualification: tests written by the same team as the checker; they find faults in the code, they do not establish independence

claims.statement: On a rooted ball, 1-WL started from (distance from root, degree in ball) and 1-WL started with only the root coloured reach the same stable partition, so the independent check (root only) and this package measure the same r_WL.
claims.reproduce: not machine-checked; the independent team also ran both initialisations for ben/cat, tsa/tsg and acl/nih and found the same results
